wordmark.purpose: The mono wordmark, with its prompt glyph in Lime.

small.purpose: Back links, the section heading link, the footer, the mobile nav, list labels. Quiet Ink.

label.purpose: Stack lists, years, the rail path, place and time, the search button and key caps, the key hint.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and opacity changes on hover, focus and selection: rail links, rows, the selection marker, tags, buttons, the terminal border.

motion.name: preview-fade
motion.purpose: The preview pane fades its new content in from opacity 0 when the selected work row changes.

motion.name: dialog
motion.purpose: The command menu and its backdrop opening and closing (stock shadcn dialog).

motion.name: arrow-nudge
motion.purpose: A trailing arrow on a linked row moves 4px right (next project) or 2px up and right (contact rows) on hover and turns lime.

motion.name: marble-fade-in
motion.purpose: The marbling canvas fades in once its first frame is drawn.

motion.name: marble-drift
motion.purpose: How fast the noise field moves, in shader time units per second.

motion.name: marble-frame-lit
motion.purpose: Frame interval while the lamp is lit.

motion.name: marble-frame-rest
motion.purpose: Frame interval once the lamp is out and only the drift is left. No frames in a hidden tab.

motion.name: lamp-contours
motion.value: 0.85 where the level is near 1, 0.3 elsewhere
motion.purpose: Strength of the lime contour lines around the lamp: full at the top of the home page, about a third where there is text to read. The lamp brightens the marbling only where the level is near 1 (smoothstep 0.82 to 1).

motion.name: lamp-follow
motion.purpose: The lamp eases after the mouse, or is placed where a finger or pen lands. It does not move on its own.

motion.name: lamp-rise
motion.purpose: The lamp comes up when the pointer moves.

motion.name: lamp-fall
motion.purpose: The lamp goes out once the pointer has rested.

motion.name: marble-level
motion.value: 1 at the top of the home page, 0.8 elsewhere
motion.purpose: Overall strength; eases from 1 to 0.8 (smoothstep) over the first 80% of a viewport height of scrolling on the home page.

motion.name: marble-budget
motion.value: 700000 pixels, at most 1.5 device pixels per CSS pixel
motion.purpose: The canvas is drawn to a pixel budget and scaled up in CSS.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: With prefers-reduced-motion every animation and transition is cut to 0.01ms, and the marbling draws one still frame (lamp at 0.6, time fixed).

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Gutters go from 1.25rem to 2rem; display type reaches full size; rows get 0.75rem side padding (work rows have none below this).

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The About section becomes two columns.

breakpoints.name: lg
breakpoints.purpose: The rail replaces the top bar; the preview pane and the row marker appear; gutters become 3rem; the content column becomes a flex column at least a screen tall so the footer rests at the bottom; case studies get the side column.

breakpoints.name: xl
breakpoints.purpose: The home page statement and the terminal share one row, 1.4fr to 1fr.

marble.lampReach: 0.09 * min(1, aspect squared), in units of the canvas height squared: a share of the shorter side

narrative.overview:
The site is laid out and operated like the tools its owner builds. A rail sits fixed on the left the way an app's sidebar does, the work is a list you move through with the keyboard, and the terminal on the home page runs real commands. It is a portfolio that behaves like software, so the evidence for "backend developer" is the page itself.

Everything sits on one continuous ground: a slow marbling drawn in WebGL, fixed behind every page and printed in three flat tones stepped from the theme's own greys. Content is placed straight onto it and separated by hairlines. There are no cards. Exactly two things have a frame: the terminal and the preview pane beside the work list. There are two themes, a warm off-white and a near-black, and both use the same tokens, the same layout and the same rules. The theme follows the system and can be toggled from the rail, the terminal or the command menu.

The mood is quiet and exact: dense enough to feel like a tool, with large tight headings and small monospace detail. Colour is nearly absent. The one accent is lime (olive-lime on the light theme, bright lime on the dark), and it marks what is live or what can be acted on, with at most one lime-filled action in view. Motion is limited to the ground drifting, the pointer's lamp, and short state changes; nothing slides or reveals itself on scroll.
keyCharacteristics: One marbled ground behind every page, in the theme's own greys; no second background anywhere.
A fixed 15rem rail from 64rem up; a two-row bar below that.
Rows separated by hairlines in place of cards; lists open with a top rule and close each row with a bottom rule.
Two framed objects only: the terminal and the preview pane, both on the card colour with a 1px border and a 10px radius.
One accent. Lime marks the live and the actionable, fills at most one action in view, and never fills a surface.
Inter at tight display settings for everything said; JetBrains Mono only for what a machine would print.
Keyboard first: arrow keys or J/K on the work list, Ctrl/⌘ K for the command menu, a visible focus ring everywhere.

rules.name: The Live Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime marks what is live or what can be acted on: the prompt, the caret, the selection marker, the current page, focus, a link's underline. Three adaptations of the direction contract are approved by the owner, who asked to keep the current style: one filled primary action, bullets in long-form text, and the `@theoreotm` handle. Lime is never a background, a heading colour, a tint or decoration.

rules.name: The One Filled Action Rule
rules.body: At most one lime-filled action in view. On the home page's first screen that is the preview pane's "Read the case study", so the two buttons under the statement are outline and ghost; the filled "Let's talk" comes at the foot of the page.

rules.name: The Theme Greys Rule
rules.body: The ground, the frames, the hairlines and the marbling are all derived from the theme's neutral tokens. No extra greys, no gradients, no second accent.

rules.name: The Faint Rule
rules.body: Faint is for marks that decorate: a prompt's `~`, a separator, the scrollbar. Anything a reader needs, however small, is Quiet Ink.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Inter says things; JetBrains Mono reports them. Mono is for what a machine would print: commands, paths, keys, times, dates, stacks, tags, handles. Navigation, back links, labels, the footer and sentences are Inter; in a sentence that contains a time, only the time is mono.

rules.name: The Tight Display Rule
rules.body: Anything 2.25rem or larger is semibold with negative tracking (-0.03em to -0.035em) and a line-height of 1.02 to 1.05. Display type is never light, never loose and never uppercase.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Every page uses the same shell, the same 68rem column and the same gutters. No page is full-bleed and no page has its own container.

rules.name: The Rail Carries It Rule
rules.body: What the rail shows from 64rem up (place, time, social links) is shown in the page or footer below 64rem, never both at once.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No shadows, no glows, no blurred panels. A thing is separated from the ground by a hairline or by space.

rules.name: The Two Frames Rule
rules.body: Only the terminal and the preview pane get a filled, bordered frame. Everything else that looks like it wants a card is a row between hairlines.

rules.name: The Square Row Rule
rules.body: Radius belongs to the two frames (10px) and to small controls (8px). A row, a rule or a section never gets rounded corners.

dos: Do put content straight on the marbled ground and separate it with 1px hairlines: a top rule on the list, a bottom rule on each row.
Do use the theme tokens for every colour, so both themes and the marbling stay in step.
Do keep lime for the live and the actionable: prompt, caret, selection marker, current page, focus ring, link underline, and at most one lime-filled action in view.
Do set anything a machine would print in JetBrains Mono (paths, keys, times, dates, stack names, tags, handles) and everything else in Inter.
Do make every list operable from the keyboard and keep the 2px lime focus ring visible.
Do keep state changes short: 150ms for colour, 200ms for the preview pane's fade.
Do leave the marbling at its quiet strength (0.8) under anything that is mostly reading, and keep its tones close enough that Quiet Ink clears 4.5:1 on the brightest.
Do repeat below 64rem, in the page or footer, whatever the rail carries above it.
Do respect reduced motion: one still frame of marbling and near-instant transitions.
donts: Don't add cards, panels or tiles. The terminal and the preview pane are the only framed objects.
Don't add shadows, glows, gradients or blurred surfaces.
Don't use lime as a background tint, a heading colour or decoration, don't put two lime-filled actions in one view, and don't add a second accent.
Don't set Faint on anything a reader needs; it is about 3.3:1 on the light ground. Use Quiet Ink.
Don't give the rail a fill, or put any background between the content and the marbling.
Don't animate on load or on scroll. Only the ground drifts.
Don't round rows, rules or sections; radius is for the two frames (10px) and small controls (8px).
Don't set sentences, navigation, back links, labels or the footer in mono.
Don't give a page its own container, width or background; every page uses the same shell.
